packageRules.description: arrow and parquet share one version number and must move together (parquet 59.x pins arrow-* ^59.x), so a bump to either alone fails resolution. Renovate PR #776 did exactly that: parquet 59.2 to 59.3 while arrow-* stayed on 59.2, because this rule matched only arrow. Grouping them lands both in one PR. Held below 60 because DataFusion 55 pins arrow/parquet ^59.2; the next major is the RFC 0021 phase-2 pattern and lifts together with the DataFusion bump that requires it.

Hold zstd at 0.13.x. The direct zstd dependency in ourios-bench and ourios-querier exists to share the copy parquet already pulls in (see their Cargo.toml comments), and parquet 59 pins zstd ^0.13. A standalone bump to 0.14 resolves, but only by adding a second zstd and zstd-safe to the tree, the opposite of why the dependency is declared (Renovate PR #776). Lift together with the parquet that requires zstd 0.14.

Hold object_store at 0.13.x. DataFusion 55 still pins object_store ^0.13.2, and ourios-querier hands ourios-parquet's Store::object_store() to DataFusion's register_object_store (RFC 0013 §2.2), so the two crates must share one object_store version. Bumping to 0.14 splits the Arc<dyn ObjectStore> type at that boundary and breaks the build. This is RFC 0021 phase 2b (epic #314): lift when a released DataFusion accepts object_store 0.14. The DataFusion 55 upgrade did not open it.

Hold reqwest at 0.12.x. reqwest 0.13 drops the rustls-tls-manual-roots feature ourios-ingester's OTLP exporter path uses, and object_store 0.12/0.13 still require reqwest ^0.12, so a standalone bump fails resolution (Renovate PR #505's plan failure). Lift together with the object_store hold above (RFC 0021 phase 2b); the DataFusion 55 upgrade did not open it, because DataFusion 55 still pins object_store 0.13.

Hold p256 at 0.13.x. jsonwebtoken pins the RustCrypto 0.13-era stack (elliptic-curve/ecdsa/pkcs8), and p256 0.14 moves to the split rand-core/pkcs8 APIs (OsRng relocation, to_pkcs8_pem removal) that broke Renovate PR #505's clippy. Lift when jsonwebtoken ships a RustCrypto-0.14-era release; run cargo tree -i p256 first.

Hold rand at 0.8.x. The test ES256 key minting feeds p256 0.13's rand_core 0.6 traits, and rand 0.9+ removes rand::rngs::OsRng (the exact break in Renovate PR #505's third regeneration). Lifts together with the p256 hold above when jsonwebtoken moves to the RustCrypto 0.14-era stack.

Don't digest-pin the chart's default image. image.tag is deliberately empty (floating latest; the values.yaml comment tells operators to pin a released tag in production), so a point-in-time digest in the published chart's defaults contradicts that contract - and renovate writes it as a bare @sha256:... tag, which the ourios.image helper renders as an invalid repo:@sha256:... reference.
